issues.description: The UML in the problem statement specifies Farm.addAnimal(animal: Animal): boolean, but the provided solution implements addAnimal(Animal) with a void return type and the template does not define the method yet. The textual task description only says "addAnimal(Animal a) adds an animal to the list" (no return type), which is ambiguous. This mismatch between the UML and the implementation/template can confuse students about whether they should implement addAnimal to return a boolean or void.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the expected signature of addAnimal consistent across artifacts. Either update the UML in problem_statement.md to show addAnimal(animal: Animal): void (and clarify in the textual description), or change the solution and template to implement addAnimal returning boolean (e.g., returning true on successful add). Ensure the template Farm.java contains the same method signature students are expected to implement.

issues.description: The UML in the problem statement declares Farm.addAnimal(animal: Animal): boolean (i.e., a boolean-returning method), but the template/solution implementation uses a void addAnimal(Animal) (the solution defines public void addAnimal(Animal)). This mismatch between the problem's UML signature and the actual code signature can confuse students about the expected return type and contract of addAnimal.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the addAnimal method signature consistent across artifacts. Either update the UML in problem_statement.md to declare addAnimal(animal: Animal): void, or change the template and solution implementations to return boolean (e.g., return true on success / false on failure) and document the semantics. Prefer updating the UML to void if no success/failure boolean is intended.
